Holy Wars

By: Jacqui Jayamaha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The unprecedented violent attack and murder of members of the Imam Husain Mosque in Verulum, has sent shock waves throughout religious communities in Durban.

Unique Selling Point:
Never in the History of South Africa has there been an act of such violence, perpetrated in a religious place of worship, such as that committed on Thursday 10th May at the Shia Imam Hussein Mosque in Verulum, Durban. Three men entered the mosque grounds posing as worshippers and proceeded to brutally attack 3 members of the Mosque in the grounds of the building. All three victims had their throats cut and bodies butchered, with 2 surviving and tragically a young father Abbas Essop succumbing to his horrific stab wounds on the way to hospital. The assailants proceeded to burn the library down which contained a collection of Holy Books including many translations of the Muslim Holy Book the Koran. After the police had "swept" the scene for evidence a canister of spray paint, a pair of glasses and a bomb device was found under the Moulana's chair in the pulpit.

Summary:
This violent attack on a Mosque is unprecedented with many in the community saying it is definitely a terrorist attack bearing all the Hallmarks of ISIS and other extremist groups that are currently in South Arica. The Moulana Aftab categorically states that this attack is due to inciting of the Sunni sect of Muslims, who make up a huge majority of Muslims, against the far smaller Shia group. Hate speech and messages on social media referring to Shia's as being enemies of Islam, have been an ongoing threat to the members of the small Shia sect - they believe is due to some differences in their application of the religion.
Besides the "Holy War" that seems to be playing out - Abbas Essop's family have been left fractured and desperate for answers. Abbas has now been martyred as in South Africa Islmaic rule - he died as he lived a hero, protecting members of his mosque.
To add to the Extremist theories - after SAPS had swept the Mosque for evidence and clues and the Mosque left open - the Carte Blanche team were allowed in to film the scene of pools of congealed blood, gas canister and burnt library. Later theMosque was again shut down to the public and a bomb device discovered under the Imam's chair. The suggestion therefore has been made that the attackers wanted to blow up the whole Mosque. We are tstill tracking the story and are been given access to the family of the deceased who want this story of bloody murder, arson and hate to be brought to the public's attention.

Press Release:


Holy Wars
Never before in South Africa’s history has there been an act of such violence in a place of worship, as the attack on the Shia Imam Hussain Mosque in Verulam, Durban.
What could have motivated three suspects, posing as worshippers, to brutally assault three people - one of whom has succumbed to his stab wounds? The suspects then burned down a library with a collection of Holy Books. Police found a spray paint can, pair of glasses and an explosive device under the Imam’s chair. Has ISIS extremism reached our shores or are there local forces fuelling the hatred?


Script:


“Holy War”
SFX – Muslim Call to prayer
Close up palm leaves in sun
Wide shot Verulum Mosque
Sound up from chanting and praying at grave
Visuals - grave and prayers.
V/O “ Mourning relatives and friends of Shaheed Abbas Essop, pray over his newly laid grave. They are still in deep shock and disbelief about the violent death he suffered.
Hailed now as a hero, he is given the title Shaheed, meaning martyr, as he died honorably protecting his brothers.
Visual cutaways poster on wall (Signage and photos - Martyred Shaheed)

Macfarlane Link “Up until the 10th of May members of this community Christian, Hindu and Muslim, both Sunni and Shi’a lived in harmony, everyone practicing their religion freely without any fear, so what happened?

V/O In act of barbaric violence, Abbas was murdered protecting 2 of his Muslim brothers. He was found with his mouth duct taped, hands bound, his throat slit and body butchered at the Imam Hussain Shi’a Mosque.
Vis Amateur footagevictims bleeding on the ground
Dramatisation – duct tape mouth, hands and knife
Wide Mosque
B roll C/U Brother of deceased, Jafer Essop in mosque

V/O “One of Abbas’ brothers, Jafer explains what happened”

Interview Jafer Essop “If you look here this is my brother’s shoe here there’s one shoe lying, this is where he was attacked. He was ambushed basically, he actually walked into an attack and they actually dragged his body, they dragged him into the kitchen here. There’s the other shoe here, if you look here, this is the blood lying right here, he was massacred here, he was slaughtered right here. There’s blood all over. This is where everything took place. You can see there was a battle for life. And this is where he bled to death..I wasn’t here to help him, I wasn’t here to defend him, I wasn’t here to stand next to him”

V/O “As abhorrent as the situation is with accusations and suspicions flying around the religious communities, it is Abbas Essop’s family, particularly his young wife, Sakina Essop and his daughters whose lives have been shattered”
Vis shots of mosques, wide family, close up widow weeps, wide

Mac “So what was he like as a father?
Sakina “As a father he was , I think I couldn’t have asked for better, he was like the perfect father, like they were his life, there was nothing they could say and he would say no”. I would always tease him that you know what, you just can’t say no to them”.
Mac How did you then break the news to the children?
Sakina ”Like I tell told my daughter that your father is always going to be there for us, he’s an angel now – he’s your guardian, he’s your protective angel – he’s always going to be there for you”.

V/O The Shi’s community believes this act was based on religious motives and executed by members of an extremist sect”

Vis b roll praying at grave at grave
V/O “Moulana Aftab Haider is convincedthat terrorism and hatred for the Shi’a Muslims was the motive behind the bloody attack.

Moulana “ Beyond any doubt it has hallmarks of Terrorism, Religious Extremism sectarianism, they did not ask for any money, they did not steal anything, they only wanted to hurt and kill – they repeatedly said to the people We want to kill you. There were threats also social media. Evens sometimes coming from community radio stations and even unfortunately from some pulpits of mosques and religious platforms. We used to promote hate.”

V/O Sunni Imam, Hafez Fuzail Soofie, leader of the Westville Mosque

Mac “Just take me through, what’s the fundamental difference between Shi’a and Sunni?
Fuzail “The issue between Sunni Muslims in South Africa and Shi’a Muslim in South Africa is no different from the ideological, theoretical differences that exist between various Christian denominations or for that matter Jewish groups or for that matter Hindu groups as well. And because there are differences in terms of the school of thought, there always will be in all religious communities academic grandstanding, religious banter, robust passionate discussions abut the ideological differences between one another and so on”.
Mac “What actually happened at the mosque in Verulum?
Fuzail “Either this is some form of a scare tactic right? Or it’s another form of, you know, trying to instigate this idea that, you know what there is something way beyond in terms of violence and so on,they way they destruction of the mosque and son on, because in 24 hours forsomething like this to have taken place without anybody finding out anything before that or getting a hold of the perpetrators – or for that matter, the Hawks after having done their investigation, not finding something – it gives you an indication that there’s something suspicious and something fishy going on”.
Mac “One cannot obviously ignore the backlash that has happened especially on social media, we’ve seen a lot of hate speech happening you know, from Sunnis to Shi’a Muslims and that has also created a lot of divisions”
Fuzail “The Sunni Muslims in the country are just as confused, just as surprised, just as shocked and just as fearful because of the negative stereotyping which comes with this. And the last thing that we need is an issue to be magnified in terms of our so-called ‘doctrinal divisions’ to become a point where they’ll be instigating ferment between communities”.

V/O “ The intruders set alight and vandalized the library, burning Holy Books, including copies of the Koran. A large gas canister in the kitchen was found opened with gas escaping, believed by the Shi’a community, to be in an attempt to blow up the entire Mosque”.
Visuals burnt library
Cutaway Library sign
Visuals – large gas canister in kitchen relative to stove, pipe etc.
Visuals from EWN crime scene Capt. Mhlongo, blue lights etc
Device pic
Cut away Moulana’s chair

V/O “24 hours after the South African Police Services, forensics and canine unit had swept the Mosque, more terror was to be visited upon the community as a home made explosive device of white piping wired to a mobile phone, was found under the pulpit chair of the Moulana, suggesting that he may have been a possible target.
Amateur footage of cops, lights
Captain Mhlongo Hawks
V/O The identity of the perpetrators has not yet been established. Capt. Mhlongo of the Hawks priority crime investigators.

Capt. Mhlongo “And it’s hard to believe that, that device was there on the date in question. Ask yourself why, if it was there for the purpose of burning of the mosque or attacking, why t never exploded or burnt the mosque on Friday when our members were there? Our members, forensic team and other role players thoroughly searched the mosque the whole day, so the issue of whether this device was there on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday till Sunday is questionable.

V/O He believes there may an element of extremism indicated in this incident.

Capt. Mhlongo “The brutal manner in which it happened anyone can see it was the extreme violence that was used on the victims. It was “elements” we are not concluding that it’s extremism. We want to investigate first and the findings of our investigation will reveal what really happened.”

V/O “First responders at the crime scene were IPSS rescue members
Operations manager Paul Hebst had never seen an attack of this nature”.
B roll Paul Hebst packs helicopter
(Footage cell phone amateur of bodies and respondents)
Paul Interview “ We’ve been into the field now for about 18 years, obviously we see stabbings and traumatic injuries on a daily basis. However the circumstances around this incident is also one of the first attacks in SA to do with religion and a place of worship. On arrival we found 3 people that were severely injured at the time. One of the people, his throat was slit and he had severed one of the main arteries in his neck. We were currently working on him in order to stabilize him, unfortunately due to his severe injuries and massive blood loss he wasmoved in a critical condition through to hospital where unfortunately he later passed away”. ”

V/O “Abbas’ Mother Farieda Essop speaks proudly of her son
Visual wide of family and close up Mother Farieda Essop

Mac” So Ma what was Abbas like as a son?”
Farieda “How do I answer that question, was a star. He was a star and I didn’t realise the depth of his greatness till after he was dead”.
Mac “So how’s this whole thing affecting you as a family, and as well as you as a mother?
Farieda “When I heard he had teeth marks on his knuckles and he was fighting with 3 of them, oh my God – I said, that’s my Abbas!! That is what he stood for and God has chosen him for that cause and I think that gives me contentment to face anything, it gave me courage”.

Macfarlane Link – The media frenzy, rumours and hate-speech have added fuel to an already volatile situation which has led to a violent and unprecedented act of terror in the South African Muslim community. Hopefully, once the perpetrators have been found, then, will we know the truth”.

Sakina “Every morning he would take both of them out to see the birds. So they would walk in the garden before he went to work”
Sakina ”He was a perfect father and as a husband as well. He made me the woman I am today – he had his way of telling me how to be awake and look around and you know…..sorry, he was a good man”.

Little Girl ”That’s my dad, he’s reading ”
Visuals little daughter listens to her dad Abbas Essop chanting on the cellphone

END (10 minutes)
